power_purchase.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves Rs.706.94 lakh as power purchase cost for the year 2022-23.
key_observations: Solar power (0.28 lakh units) purchased from prosumer approved at Rs.0.75 lakh (against claimed Rs.0.83 lakh) based on APPC @Rs.2.69/unit.
Efficiency gain of Rs.3.45 lakh due to lower distribution loss, with Rs.2.30 lakh retained by licensee (2/3rd) and Rs.1.15 lakh passed on to consumers (1/3rd).
power_purchase.methodology_applied: Regulation 73(3) for sharing efficiency gain from distribution loss; APPC for solar power purchase.

employee_cost.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves the employee expenses of Rs.23.53 lakh based on actual inflation rate for the year 2022-23 against the licensee's claim of Rs.24.99 lakh.
key_observations: Increase in employee cost mainly due to deployment of separate Resident Engineer to Infopark Phase-II.
Medical reimbursement expenses increased by Rs.2.14 lakh in 2022-23 from Rs.1.46 lakh in 2021-22.
Commission recommends exploring medical insurance for the 3 employees.
employee_cost.methodology_applied: Actual inflation rate (7.06%) applied to base year O&M norms as per Annexure-7 of Tariff Regulations, 2021.

repair_maintenance.kserc_reasoning: The Commission after considering the details in the petition and clarifications submitted by the licensee as well as comments of KSEB Ltd, hereby approves Rs.35.57 lakh (Rs.24.81 lakh+ Rs.10.67 lakh) as R&M expenses for the year 2022-23.
key_observations: KSEB Ltd commented that most claimed one-time repair works are routine.
Only Replacement of Lightning Arrestor at Cherthala (Rs.3.16 lakh) was considered eligible for one-time repair works by KSEB Ltd.

Approved one-time expenses: Transformer painting (Rs.2.72 lakh), Replacement of LA at Cherthala (Rs.3.16 lakh), 110 KV Switchyard painting (Rs.3.81 lakh), Cable cellar painting at 220 KV substation (Rs.0.98 lakh), totaling Rs.10.67 lakh.
repair_maintenance.methodology_applied: Actual inflation rate (7.06%) applied to base year O&M norms for routine R&M, plus specific one-time expenses allowed after prudence check as per Regulation 80(3).

admin_general.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves an amount of Rs.6.04 lakh (Rs.4.80 lakh + Rs.1.24 lakh) including one-time expense, as the A&G expenses for the year 2022-23.
key_observations: Increased A&G expenses due to ABT meter testing fee, training fees, consultant fees, and increased insurance premium.
Approved one-time expenses: Training fees at KSEB Ltd (Rs.0.14 lakh) and other professional fees (Rs.1.10 lakh), totaling Rs.1.24 lakh.
admin_general.methodology_applied: Actual inflation rate (7.06%) applied to base year O&M norms for routine A&G, plus specific one-time expenses allowed.

depreciation.kserc_reasoning: The Commission hereby approves depreciation of Rs.47.21 lakh for the year 2022-23 as claimed by the licensee.
key_observations: Claim is in line with the provisions of the Tariff Regulations, 2021.
No depreciation claimed for capital expenditure met out of Government grant.
depreciation.methodology_applied: Straight-line method in line with the Tariff Regulations, 2021.

interest_long_term.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, the interest on normative loan approved by the Commission for the year 2022-23 is Rs.48.36 lakh.
key_observations: Licensee's actual loan portfolio was repaid by 2017.
Interest rate based on External Benchmark-Linked Lending Rate (EBLR) of SBI as on 01-04-2022 (6.65%).
interest_long_term.methodology_applied: Regulation 29(4) of Tariff Regulations 2021, applying base rate (EBLR) when no actual loan portfolio.

interest_consumer_deposits.kserc_reasoning: The Commission examined the submission and approves Rs.4.26 lakh as claimed by the licensee towards the Interest on security deposits and Bank charges.
key_observations: Reduction in interest rate is the reason for the decrease in interest on security deposit compared to the previous year.
interest_consumer_deposits.methodology_applied: Approved as claimed with minor adjustment.

return_on_nfa.kserc_reasoning: Accordingly, the Commission hereby approves Return on Net Fixed Assets of Rs.41.30 lakh for the year 2022-23.
key_observations: Increase in claim compared to previous year due to change in the rate of return.
Return allowed at 5.50 percent on the net fixed assets at the beginning of the financial year.

energy_decision.kserc_reasoning: Considering the fact that the licensee has achieved a distribution loss better than the distribution loss approved by the Commission, the Commission hereby approves the actual loss of 3.93% achieved by the licensee. The licensee shall take added efforts to reduce the losses further. Accordingly, the efficiency gain on distribution loss has to be shared in the ratio of 2:1 between the licensee and consumers i.e., 2/3rd of gain is to be retained by the licensee and 1/3rd is to be passed on to the consumers.
energy_decision.excess_demand_action: Efficiency gain on distribution loss of Rs.3.45 lakh is shared in the ratio of 2:1 between the licensee (Rs.2.30 lakh) and consumers (Rs.1.15 lakh).

capital_structure_verified.kserc_reasoning: The licensee in the petition has considered the asset addition of Rs.47.61 lakh towards expenditure with regard to major replacement and repair work on the 220 kV Siemens Gas Insulated Switchgear which has already been approved by the Commission while truing up the accounts for the year 2021-22. During the year 2022-23, the licensee has not made any assets additions.
